context:
Inventory first, then classify. Only after the claim classes are explicit,
implement a narrow drift check that targets current public source files. Avoid
a naive repository-wide grep gate that fails on historical evidence or build
artifacts. Fix stale public claims in the same PR so the new gate lands green.
description:
PR #502 updated the public contract map and MCP docs, but review found other
public surfaces that still carry hand-maintained benchmark breadth claims such
as "22 benchmarks" or exact coverage counts. README has a registry-backed
marker, but landing copy, architecture docs, CLI utility docs, and development
docs can still drift from benchmark registry metadata and support-status
policy.

Add a compact drift gate for public benchmark count and support claims. The
gate should distinguish authoritative registry-derived claims from editorial
examples, and it should make stale exact counts visible before release. This
work should not force all narrative docs to become generated; it should define
where exact public claims are allowed and how they are checked.

anti_patterns.dont: add a global grep that scans docs/_build or _project history
anti_patterns.why: historical/generated text will create noisy false positives

anti_patterns.dont: hard-code counts in a new script without deriving expected values from the registry
make README the only checked surface
anti_patterns.instead: include the durable public source files found in w0.
anti_patterns.why: landing and reference docs are also public

anti_patterns.dont: replace useful explanatory copy with generated blobs
anti_patterns.instead: check exact counts and source-of-truth claims only.

deferrals.reason: docs/usage/ is outside this TODO's scope_limit. faq.md:32 says 'eighteen benchmarks' (stale; registry has 22 public). Repair it and extend test_public_benchmark_count_claims_are_registry_derived to cover faq.md in a follow-up that includes docs/usage/.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] obsolete: Spot-checked: 'eighteen benchmarks' string is no longer present in docs — the stale claim has already been fixed.
deferrals.summary: Fix stale 'eighteen benchmarks' claim in docs/usage/faq.md and add it to the drift gate

preserves.behavior: Editorial benchmark examples can remain narrative if they avoid exact authoritative count claims.
Generated docs under docs/_build remain excluded from source drift checks.
Historical DONE/TODO records are not rewritten just because they contain old count evidence.
README registry count markers remain checked against runtime metadata.

prior_art.concept: .github/workflows/pr.yml: public contract source-derived claim check - extend or mirror for benchmark claim fragments.
README.md: benchbox-registry-counts marker block - preserve as authoritative user-facing count source.
docs/reference/public-contracts.md: Count and Drift Policy - extend claim-class rules instead of scattering policy language.
tests/unit/core/test_benchmark_api_contract.py: benchmark API snapshot marker - reuse registry-derived counts for benchmark-specific assertions.
tests/unit/core/test_platform_registry.py: README and platform docs count marker tests - reuse marker-check pattern for public benchmark claims.

verifications.description: Benchmark contract tests cover the new drift check.
Docs validation remains green after public claim edits.
PR public contract workflow snippet remains syntactically valid through the fast unit lane.

work_units.notes:
Search for phrases such as "22 benchmarks", "23 benchmark", "registered
benchmarks", "supported benchmarks", "benchmark variety", and benchmark
support/status vocabulary. Classify each hit as authoritative,
registry-derived, editorial example, stale, generated output, or internal
planning context. Exclude `docs/_build/` and generated index artifacts.
work_units.summary: Inventory exact benchmark count, coverage, and support-claim text across public docs, landing pages, scripts, and generated docs sources

work_units.notes:
Extend the public contract map or a nearby developer doc with concrete
rules: exact public counts must be registry-derived or checked; editorial
examples may avoid exact totals; generated outputs must state their
generator; internal TODO/DONE history does not create public contract.
work_units.summary: Define allowed claim classes and source-of-truth rules

work_units.notes:
Prefer extending an existing lightweight docs/contract test over adding a
broad fragile scanner. The check should cover durable public surfaces such
as README markers, landing source copy, architecture docs, CLI reference
docs, and result-integrity coverage docs. It should report file paths and
the stale phrase or missing registry-derived marker.
work_units.summary: Implement a focused drift check for benchmark count and support-status claims

work_units.notes:
Update exact count claims to derive from the registry-backed marker where
practical. Where exact counts are not important, reword copy to avoid a
brittle total. Do not update historical TODO/DONE files unless they are
being used as current public documentation.
work_units.summary: Repair stale public claims or reword them as editorial examples

work_units.notes:
Place the check where maintainers already expect public contract drift to
fail, such as a unit contract test or the existing PR public-contract gate.
Keep failure output concise and redirect any large inventory output to
`/tmp` or a generated local artifact that is not committed.
work_units.summary: Wire the drift check into the narrowest existing verification lane
